description: trail-blazer-flow: two PreToolUse Bash hooks. (1) git-c-guard.sh approves only the exact git -C <worktree> <subcommand> forms worktree-parallel mode issues (see issue #150); says nothing about everything else, so the normal permission flow -- a prompt, or a matching deny rule, which always wins over this hook's decision -- applies. Its if gate (#155, Claude Code 2.1.85+) restricts when it is even spawned to git -C Bash calls; it can only reduce spawns, never widen approval. (2) agent-boundary.sh (#235) mechanically enforces the implementer/verifier subagents' git/gh boundary from stdin's agent_type field -- a role the if gate cannot see, since if is permission-rule syntax over tool_input only, so this handler carries no if key at all (any if here would silence the boundary for exactly the commands it exists to block; it is spawned for every Bash call, with its own raw-stdin fast paths keeping the common case cheap). Composition between the two hooks for the same call is unverified -- see hooks/agent-boundary.sh's header.
